answer: Stake-floor with linear influence resists sybils: each identity must lock a minimum bond, and voting influence is strictly linear in stake with no per-head bonus, so splitting one pool of capital across a knoll of fakes yields the same total influence as one identity — the velvet promise of amplification by division never arrives. N fakes lock N minimum floors for zero aggregate gain; an honest agent posts one bond. The signal is plain: extra identities are pure cost. Precondition: influence has no convex per-identity component and the floor is enforced per head.
